newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Airport Authority fine-tuning HK$5 bln facility.
newsitem.headline: HK Airport Authority fine-tuning HK$5 bln facility.

text.p: The Hong Kong Airport Authority (AA) said it is finalising a new HK$5 billion facility to help fund the territory's new Chek Lap Kok airport.

"The Authority is now in the final legal documentation stage of establishing a note-issuance programme to be arranged and mandated by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA)," the AA said in its annual report released this week.
The AA is charged with building and operating the new airport, which is due to open in April 1998.
It said the programme size could be increased at any time with the agreement of the HKMA.
Notes with different coupons could be issued under the programme, including some with access to the liquidity adjustment facility operated by the HKMA, it said.
"This programme will become a key domestic source of the Authority's long-term fixed interest rate funding," it said.
The AA said it expected to draw down on its HK$8.2 billion syndicated loan or start note issuance towards the end of 1997.

It added that it had entered into a series of interest rate swap contracts for a total notional principal of HK$4 billion to hedge its interest rate exposure during the construction of the airport, through to March 31, 1999.
